mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% q/q over the last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by >2% y/y.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which increases input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four-month stretches of INDPRO below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflationary environment, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases uncertainty, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong, persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market optimism, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during three-month stretches where HOUST is above its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (i.e., more people employed but unemployment still rising) over two months signals labor market churning or underemployment, which depresses wage growth and consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise over two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and weaker consumption momentum, which reduces near-term demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during six-month stretches where RSAFS is above its 12-month MA.
